Caption edited based on feedback in the comments! The video overstates it: airstones do add a little oxygen directly, but most of the benefit comes from circulation and surface agitation. A common misconception in the aquarium hobby is that airstone bubbles oxygenate your tank by dissolving oxygen as they rise. In reality, most of the benefit comes from two other things. First, circulation. Rising bubbles lift oxygen-poor water from the bottom up to the surface. Second, surface agitation. Gas exchange happens at the surface, so more ripple means more surface area for oxygen to get in and CO2 to get out. The bubbles themselves add a little oxygen, but it's a small share of the total. If you want better aeration, aim your filter output or a spray bar to ripple the surface steadily. Airstones still help, they just do it indirectly. Bear in mind some fish (bettas, shrimp, many shy species) dislike strong flow, so adjust to your stock. #FishKeeping #AquariumTips #Aquascape #FishTank

Must haves for your tank. Tap water conditioner and Sludge destroyer. The additives in tap water suck as chlorine are harmful to your babies. Chlorine can cause health issues and deformities to your turtles shell, this is why you use water conditioner. If you have a large tank, get the super strength water conditioner, smaller tanks like a 20 or 40 gallon tank, you can start off with regular strength. You also need to have the sludge destroyer. This helps break down waste and debris like food particles in the tank. To be clear, sludge destroyer is a clearish liquid that has good bacteria to help your tank. With every water change, you want to add these to your tank. I hope this helps someone who is new to turtle life! #turtle #update #todo #aquaticlife #happyfriday
